A1.justification: Both nine-page PDFs describe the same gaze-calibration study. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison across layout shifts. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section VII, Tables I–IV, and Figures 4–5 report original calibration experiments on MPIIGaze and RTGene under four training/calibration/testing scenarios.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including calibration errors, prediction ranges, and comparisons with two uncalibrated baselines.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same heteroskedastic gaze predictor, eye-image and head-angle inputs, training losses, and secondary isotonic-regression calibration procedure in Section IV.

E1.justification: MPIIGaze and RTGene remain the evaluated datasets. The four scenarios combining same/cross-dataset training and same/cross-subject calibration and testing are unchanged.

E2.justification: Both retain the uncalibrated heteroskedastic model and uncalibrated quantile-regression model trained with pinball loss. Their participation in the corresponding comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections V–VI retain ResNet-18/50, three-fold evaluation, 50 training epochs, the same calibration sampling, 95% intervals, joint pitch/yaw inclusion, and RMSE and prediction-range metrics.

E4.justification: The domain-shift comparisons, reliability-curve case study in Figure 4, and overall error-distribution analysis in Figure 5 are unchanged. Relocating Figure 4 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Fold averaging and the existing error-distribution box plot remain unchanged. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty estimates for aggregate performance, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All values in Tables I–IV and all plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table I retains MPII/ResNet-18 RMSE values of 0.076 for calibrated, 0.579 for uncalibrated, and 0.581 for pinball predictions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the Gaussian and monotonicity assumptions, calibration objective, and runtime-complexity statements are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the lightweight calibration contribution and four-scenario benchmark claims. The conclusion rewrite preserves the claims about calibration effectiveness and the importance of matching calibration and testing domains.

C2.justification: The revised conclusion restates the existing interpretation that training-domain shifts mainly increase prediction uncertainty while having limited influence on calibration accuracy. Explanations of domain mismatch, overconfidence, and cross-subject underconfidence remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The PyTorch implementation, cited data normalization, learning-rate schedule, batch size, and calibration-sample details are unchanged. No technical instructions or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 23 works and research positioning are retained. Reference [10] gains venue, volume, issue, and year information, completing an existing citation rather than introducing new related work.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and spelling corrections and rewrites the concluding sentences. It removes Jiucai Zhang from the author list and changes the running header. Section order and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figure images and four table structures are retained. Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 7 beside its discussion, surrounding text reflows, and Figure 1's caption drops the approximate 90% example.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects language errors, completes reference [10], and places Figure 4 beside its discussion in Section VII.B. These changes modestly improve readability and navigation; the method, experimental evidence, and substantive conclusions remain unchanged.
